Keppel DC REIT to Buy Stake in Japan Data Centers, Plans Equity Fundraising
By Megan Cheah
SINGAPORE--Keppel DC REIT has agreed to acquire a majority stake in two Japanese data centers, aiming to partially fund the transaction through a private placement.

The Singapore real-estate investment trust will hold a nearly 89% effective stake in the two freehold data centers upon the deal's completion, Keppel DC REIT said Tuesday. Its sponsor, Keppel Ltd., will hold around 1.4% stake in the assets.

Keppel DC REIT will pay around 168.4 billion yen, equivalent to US$1.05 billion, for its effective interest, it said, and intends to fund the acquisition through a mix of equity and yen-denominated debt.
The REIT added that it plans to raise at least 600 million Singapore dollars, equivalent to US$472.1 million, in gross proceeds from a private placement.
The units will be priced between S$2.096 and S$2.142, representing a 2.5% to 4.6% discount to the volume-weighed average price of Keppel DC REIT shares on Monday, prior to the agreement.
Loh Hwee Long, chief executive of Keppel DC REIT's manager, said the deal will deepen the trust's exposure to Japan's data center market while providing embedded growth through rent increases.
The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter.
Keppel DC REIT units last closed 0.45% lower at S$2.20 on Monday, before trading in its securities was halted.
